punchline: Gabor Maté's pediatrician told his mother that all his Jewish babies were crying; Maté counts that year as the background of his own attention problems.
thirty_sec: Gabor Maté was a baby in Budapest in 1944. His mother called the pediatrician about a baby who had cried for a day; the doctor said all his Jewish babies were crying. Later she gave Maté to a stranger for three weeks. Maté, who has ADD himself, uses this as an illustration of how early stress shapes the brain and admits he cannot prove it.
